docs.filterChip.a11y.disabled: disabled leaves the tab order, dims the chip and shows a cursor of not allowed. A button has no read-only state.
docs.filterChip.a11y.focus: The focus ring is the one of Button: it shows with the keyboard and not on a click, and it is never removed.
docs.filterChip.a11y.group: A row of toggles needs a role="group" with an aria-label or aria-labelledby that says what it filters. The name is yours, in the language of your page: the library has no text for it. The exclusivity (one pressed at a time) is your state.
docs.filterChip.a11y.modes: aria-haspopup with any value but false makes it the trigger of a popup; without it, it is a toggle. Nothing else changes the mode.
docs.filterChip.a11y.native: It is a native button: Tab reaches it, Space and Enter press it, and its text is its accessible name. type is button unless you set it.
docs.filterChip.a11y.popup: A popup trigger adds no aria-pressed, because a button that opens something is not a toggle. Give it aria-expanded and, if it has one, aria-controls. Its chevron is hidden from screen readers; selected only paints the chip, so put the applied value in the label, such as «Status: Open».
docs.filterChip.a11y.pressed: A toggle announces selected as aria-pressed, which the component always sets. It is not a prop: type refuses it, and one that arrives at run time is ignored, so that the state has one source.
docs.filterChip.a11y.strings: FilterChip has no text of its own: the label and the name of the group are yours, and a FormaProvider changes nothing here.
docs.filterChip.a11y.target: A chip is 36 px tall, and 44 px below 768 px of width, so that a finger can reach it. A pressed chip changes its border and its colors, not only its color.
docs.filterChip.api.ariaHaspopup: Chooses the mode. Any value but false makes the chip the trigger of a popup, with a chevron and no aria-pressed.
docs.filterChip.api.others: Every other attribute of the native button goes to it as it is: disabled, onClick, aria-expanded, aria-* and ref. It takes no aria-pressed, which comes from selected.
docs.filterChip.api.selected: Marks the filter as applied. A toggle announces it as pressed; a popup trigger only changes its look, so its label must carry the value.
docs.filterChip.api.type: Native. It is button unless you set it, so a chip in a form does not submit it.
docs.filterChip.group.description: A row of toggles with one pressed at a time, without panels. The group has a name that you give it, and the state that says which chip is pressed lives in your component: press one here and the others let go.
docs.filterChip.group.disabledHint: A disabled option is skipped by Tab and cannot be pressed.
docs.filterChip.group.hint: Tab reaches each chip, and Space or Enter presses it.
docs.filterChip.group.title: Single-choice row
docs.filterChip.limit.color: A pressed chip differs from the others by its border and its colors, which the pair of blue-ink and blue-bg makes distinct, and by aria-pressed. It has no check mark.
docs.filterChip.limit.design: The component comes from Resolve, where it is the trigger of a menu. The toggle mode and the focus ring are additions of Forma UI, and the chip is measured to 36 px with the border included, where Resolve's was 38 px.
docs.filterChip.limit.group: There is no component for the group: the role="group", its name, the layout of the row and which chip is pressed are yours. The example above is the whole pattern.
docs.filterChip.limit.menu: There is no menu or popover to go with a popup chip yet. The application opens and closes what the chip points at, and sets aria-expanded.
docs.filterChip.limit.pressed: A chip in popup mode never announces selected. If the same chip must toggle and open something, it is two controls.
docs.filterChip.limit.size: There is one size: 36 px high, and 44 px below 768 px of width.
docs.filterChip.popup.description: With aria-haspopup the chip does not choose anything itself: it opens the options, which your application draws. Here a Dialog does it; a menu or a popover of your own works the same way.
docs.filterChip.popup.hint: Choose a status in the dialog: the chip shows it and takes the selected look. Focus returns to the chip when the dialog closes.
docs.filterChip.popup.title: Trigger of a popup
docs.filterChip.state.disabledHint: It leaves the tab order, ignores a click and is dimmed.
docs.filterChip.state.popupHint: It opens something: a chevron, and no aria-pressed. Add aria-expanded yourself.
docs.filterChip.state.popupSelectedHint: A value is applied: selected only changes how it looks, and it still announces nothing as pressed.
docs.filterChip.state.selectedHint: Pressed: aria-pressed="true", with the selected colors and border.
docs.filterChip.state.toggleHint: Not pressed: aria-pressed="false", and no chevron.
docs.filterChip.states.description: The states that FilterChip has today, in its two modes. Without aria-haspopup it is a toggle button; with it, it is the trigger of something your application opens. Disabled is a state of its own.
docs.filterChip.summary: A filter control on a native button. It is a toggle in a row of choices, or the trigger of a popup of options, depending on aria-haspopup.
docs.filterChip.usage.description: Import FilterChip and put one for each option in a role="group" that has a name, written in your language. Each chip is pressed or not through selected, and your state decides which one is: the library keeps none.
